text: dsh-think-strip 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的上下文管理插件，通过会话消息投影从历史上下文中移除 reasoning 块，并把超过阈值的纯文本工具结果替换为头尾预览和归档路径；原文按时间戳写入本地归档并建立索引。聊天输入框旁提供独立的思考与工具开关，配置可控制默认状态、摘要和压缩长度，适合需要延长会话并减少重复上下文的用户。

dsh-think-strip reduces DSH Web context by projecting out historical reasoning and replacing long plain-text tool results with previews. It archives originals locally with an index. Per-session switches beside the composer control each behavior, while configuration sets defaults and preview sizes.
想让 DSH 长会话少带一些旧的思考内容。
能不能把很长的工具输出压成预览，同时保留原文供之后查找？
我想在聊天输入框旁分别开关思考记录和工具结果的处理。
让 DSH 把历史 reasoning 归档，只在上下文里留摘要。
How can I archive old reasoning blocks to keep a long DSH session smaller?
Can I shorten large tool results while keeping their originals searchable on disk?
dsh-think-strip 的功能「历史思考归档」：在回合结束时扫描会话历史，把 reasoning 内容写入本地文件，并通过消息投影从模型上下文中移除，可选保留首行摘要。
dsh-think-strip 的功能「长工具结果压缩」：对超过配置阈值且全为文本块的工具结果保存原文，并以头尾预览和归档路径替换上下文内容；含图片等块的结果跳过。
dsh-think-strip 的功能「逐会话开关」：Web 聊天输入框旁显示思考与工具两个开关，读取并更新当前会话状态。
dsh-think-strip 的功能「本地归档索引」：归档每条原始思考或工具结果为 JSON 文件，并向 index.jsonl 追加可搜索的条目。
dsh-think-strip 使用前须知：被剥离的内容会写入本机归档目录；关闭归档时未成功归档的内容不会被投影移除。
dsh-think-strip 使用前须知：工具结果仅在内容全部为文本块时压缩，含图片、文件或结构化块的结果会跳过。
dsh-think-strip 使用前须知：会话投影由插件提供，移除插件后，依赖该投影的会话可能无法继续派生。
希望大工具输出不要一直占用后续对话上下文。
I want per-session controls for trimming old thoughts and large tool responses.

dsh-think-strip README · dsh-think-strip：[](https://github.com/miao-pa-si-wutao/dsh-think-strip/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)

**Keep DeepSeek Harness conversations alive for hundreds of turns without paying for the same reasoning text twice.**

dsh-think-strip README · dsh-think-strip：This plugin strips historical **reasoning blocks** and **oversized tool outputs** out of the model's context. Originals are archived to disk by timestamp with a searchable index; in their place the model sees a one-line summary (for reasoning) or a head/tail preview plus the archive path (for tool results).

Two per-session switches sit left of the chat composer — **thinking** and **tools** — and they are independent. New sessions follow configured defaults.

dsh-think-strip README · dsh-think-strip：> Interface language: the plugin ships English and Chinese strings (`locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json`). Documentation: [English](README.md) · [中文](README.zh.md)

---

dsh-think-strip README · The problem：Every request DeepSeek Harness sends includes the full history: assistant `reasoning` blocks are replayed verbatim (no filter in `dsh-llm-deepseek`'s `assistant()`), and tool results are resent whole. Nothing is wrong with that per se — it is what makes an agent coherent. It is also what makes long sessions expensive and eventually impossible.

Measured on one real session (`session-f0b74f94`, 1101 tool results / 1118 assistant messages):

dsh-think-strip README · The problem：| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Total tool-output characters | 2,163,722 |
| Tool results ≥ 4000 chars | 128 results, 1,426,922 chars (**66%** of all tool text) |
| Reasoning blocks | 776 blocks, 1,078,446 chars |
| `tool/result` content shapes | `text` × 1069, `text,image` × 32 |

A handful of large tool outputs dominate the budget. Strip those 128 results and you reclaim ~1.22M characters; strip the reasoning and you reclaim another ~1.08M. Neither number is a rounding error.

dsh-think-strip README · What it guarantees：- **The append-only session log is never rewritten.** Originals stay in `session.v4.jsonl.zstd`, so fork / resume / replay behave exactly as before.
- **Prompt-cache prefixes survive.** Stripping happens mid-history, but once a strip is committed the message sequence is byte-stable, so prefix caching keeps hitting.
- **Nothing is lost.** Each stripped item is written as its own JSON file, indexed in `index.jsonl`, and the replacement text in context names the archive path — the model can go read it when it actually needs the detail.

dsh-think-strip README · How it works：Two cooperating channels, neither of which touches the log:

1. `appendPluginRecord(session, 'plugin:think-strip', { targets, indexed })` — writes one `ignorable: true` plugin record. It never enters the surface nodes and survives a DSH restart.
2. `ctx.sessions.registerMessageProjection({ type: 'plugin:think-strip', project })` — registers the matching projection. On fold, the `seq`s named by the record are replaced with **frozen copies** (each keeps its original `message.id`).

dsh-think-strip README · How it works：Each entry in `targets` is `{ seq, kind, summary?, replacement? }`, where `kind` is `'reasoning'` or `'tool'`. **Records without a `kind` are read as `'reasoning'`**, so records written by v0.1 keep working and old sessions do not break on upgrade.

Timing: on `agent/turn-stopping` (the turn is closing and the model owes no reply) the plugin rescans **all** history, archives originals first, then commits a single record covering every target `seq`.

dsh-think-strip README · How it works：Rescanning everything rather than only the current turn matters: turns from before the plugin was enabled — or before a switch was flipped — have accumulated originals that would otherwise sit in context forever. Already-processed messages come back from `session.deriveEventMessage(event)` without their originals (the projection is applied), so they are skipped for free. `session.surface.nodes` doubles as a whitelist, skipping messages already hidden by compaction.

dsh-think-strip README · Why not some other seam：| Candidate | Why it does not work |
| --- | --- |
| `agent/pre-step` to rewrite `messages` | That array holds only the user batch claimed for this step; history is not in it (`dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:902-927`, `this.inbox.claim(...)`) |
| Surface replace on `assistant/message` | Hard-rejected by the kernel: `assistant/message embeds its source stream and cannot carry sourceEventSeqs` |
| `llm/stream` waterfall mutating `options.messages` | The request is deep-frozen — "listeners read it, never rewrite it" |
| `agent/request` waterfall | Documented as unable to mutate messages |
| Plain `session.append()` with a custom type | A normal append cannot set `ignorable`; reopening the session rejects unknown events |
| The built-in `tool-result-pruner` | Broken in this DSH build: it reads `event.data.message.content[0].content` (assuming nesting) while the real shape is a flat `ContentBlock[]`, so `pruneContent(undefined)` throws. It is also `disabled: true` at `cordis.yml:321` |

dsh-think-strip README · The two session switches：Precedence: **session override > `defaults` > Config**. A switch only decides whether *this turn* commits new strip records; **records already committed keep applying forever** (the log cannot be rewritten — that is the design). To undo stripping for a session you must archive that session, or accept that it stays projected.

Query and update over HTTP (loopback only):

```powershell
dsh-think-strip README · read：Invoke-RestMethod 'http://127.0.0.1:<DSH_WEB_PORT>/think-strip/state?sessionId=session-f0b74f94'

dsh-think-strip README · tools:null clears the override and falls back to the default：Invoke-RestMethod 'http://127.0.0.1:<DSH_WEB_PORT>/think-strip/state?sessionId=session-f0b74f94' `
  -Method Post -ContentType 'application/json' -Body '{"reasoning":false}'
```
section: tools:null clears the override and falls back to the default

dsh-think-strip README · Archive layout：```
<archiveDir>/
├── switches.json                    # per-session switches
├── index.jsonl                      # one index line per archived item
├── plugin.log                       # startup marker (did apply even run?)

One archived reasoning item:

```json
{
  "kind": "reasoning",
  "time": 1760950000000,
  "sessionId": "session-f0b74f94",

One archived tool result:

```json
{
  "kind": "tool",
  "time": 1760950000000,
  "sessionId": "session-f0b74f94",

An index line:

dsh-think-strip README · Archive layout：```json
{"time":1760950000000,"sessionId":"session-f0b74f94","kind":"tool","turn":3,"step":1,"seq":97,"toolName":"pwsh","chars":49932,"summary":"pwsh output, 49932 chars","file":"session-f0b74f94/2026-10-20T10-33-24-456Z-tool-97.json"}
```

Searching it:

```powershell
dsh-think-strip README · by keyword：Select-String -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\think-archive\index.jsonl" -Pattern "some keyword"

dsh-think-strip README · tool outputs only, largest first：Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\think-archive\index.jsonl" |
  ForEach-Object { $_ | ConvertFrom-Json } |
  Where-Object { $_.kind -eq 'tool' } |
  Sort-Object chars -Descending |
  Select-Object -First 20
```

What the model sees in place of an oversized tool result:

```
(head N characters)
…[tool output archived]…
(full 49932 characters archived at: <DSH_HOME>\think-archive\session-xxx\2026-….json; read or grep it)
…(tail M characters)
```
dsh-think-strip README · tool outputs only, largest first：It reads that file when it needs the detail. What is saved is the *indiscriminate* context cost, not the information.

dsh-think-strip README · Install：From inside DSH:

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=<absolute path to this package>
```

Or add it to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by hand:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-think-strip
      name: 'dsh-think-strip'
```

The client half is declared by `package.json`'s `dsh.client.platform = "web"` plus `exports["./client"]`; the host injects it into the Web UI automatically.

dsh-think-strip README · Configuration：Set it in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, overriding by id:

```yaml
- id: dsh-think-strip
  config:
    enabled: true
    archiveDir: ''

dsh-think-strip README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. Off stops processing new turns; already-committed records still apply |
| `archiveDir` | `''` | Archive root; empty means `<DSH_HOME>/think-archive` |
| `archive` | `true` | Write originals to disk. Off strips without archiving (not recommended: items that fail to archive are not projected) |
| `summaryMode` | `first-line` | `first-line` takes the first line of the reasoning; `none` leaves only a `[reasoning archived]` stub |
| `summaryMaxChars` | `100` | Maximum summary length |
| `minReasoningChars` | `0` | Reasoning shorter than this is left alone |
| `keepSummary` | `true` | Insert a summary line where content was stripped |
| `reasoningDefault` | `true` | Default for sessions with no override |
| `toolsDefault` | `true` | Default for sessions with no override |
| `toolStripChars` | `4000` | Compress plain-text tool results longer than this; `0` compresses all |
| `toolHeadChars` | `1200` | Head characters kept after compressing |
| `toolTailChars` | `400` | Tail characters kept after compressing |
| `trace` | `true` | Write one line per turn to `plugin

dsh-think-strip README · Caveats：- **The projection lives in the plugin.** Uninstalling it makes sessions that used it refuse to derive further (`session message projection "plugin:think-strip" was removed or replaced`). To uninstall, archive those sessions first or accept that they can no longer be opened.
- **One record per turn, not per step.** Multiple steps in a turn are covered by the same record.
- **Tool results are only processed when they are entirely `text` blocks.** Results containing images / files / structured blocks (32 of 1101 measured were `text,image`) are skipped whole — splitting image blocks risks more than it saves.
- **Content that fails to archive is not projected.** Those `seq`s stay in context with a warning logged — better to spend the tokens than to lose the original.
- When compaction replaces a span of history with a summary, the hidden `seq`s are no longer on the surface and the projection silently skips them.
- **Plugin records must contain no `undefined` values.** `Session.append` validates with `snapshotJsonValue`, which only accepts booleans / strings / finite numbers / plain objects / plain arrays; a single `undefined` throws `session event "…" c

dsh-think-strip README · Tests：The pure logic layer (`lib/pure.js`) runs without Harness:

```powershell
cd dsh-think-strip
node --test test/pure.test.mjs
```
